challenges.title: Recall checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Without reopening the lesson, explain Tenfold SWE Training Expansion in your own words. Include the problem it solves, the core mechanism, and one boundary or failure.
challenges.hint: Use “Phase 1: Runtime, workflow, and test foundations” as a cue, then close the lesson again.

challenges.title: Prediction checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Choose one example or source file from this mission. Predict its behavior for a normal input and a changed or invalid input before running or revealing the reference. Explain the rule separating the outcomes.
challenges.hint: Change one condition at a time so the result teaches a rule.

challenges.title: Build and prove checkpoint
challenges.prompt: Implement, debug, or adapt the mission exercise yourself. Record the acceptance criterion, command or interaction used to verify it, failure evidence, and one tradeoff. Do not paste the reference solution.
challenges.hint: A passing check, measured result, focused diff, or reproducible demo is stronger than ‘done.’

# 180-Session Adaptive SWE Plan

This plan supplies 180 focused sessions rather than 180 consecutive calendar
days. Use 3–6 sessions per week. A standard session is 45–60 minutes; use the
short version in [the pacing guide](../ACCESSIBILITY-AND-PACING.md) when needed.

Every session begins with a no-notes prediction and ends with evidence plus a
scheduled retrieval. `R` means retrieval, `B` build, `D` debug, `M` map/model,
`E` explain, and `V` review.

## Adaptation rules

- If a session scores 0, repeat it with a smaller example and progressive hints.
- If it scores 1, retry within two days using a different input.
- If it scores 2, continue and schedule one-week retrieval.
- If it scores 3, replace the repeat with a ten-lens transfer variant.
- If time is short, preserve retrieval, one artifact, and scheduling; continue
  implementation next session.
- Every tenth session, review whether your activities overuse one learning mode.

## Phase completion rule

Do not advance only because session numbers are checked. Use the
[mastery rubric](../FEEDBACK-AND-MASTERY-RUBRIC.md), preserve the named evidence,
and repeat the weakest high-value task after a delay.

# Twenty SWE Interview Circuits

Each circuit combines retrieval, implementation or design, debugging, and
communication. Run one circuit in 60–90 minutes. A partner can act as
interviewer; solo learners should record responses and review them after a
delay.

## Scoring

Score 0–3 for:

- requirement clarification;
- correctness and edge cases;
- evidence and testing;
- debugging method;
- tradeoff reasoning;
- communication under follow-up.

Do not score memorized vocabulary. Give credit for explicit uncertainty and a
sound experiment.

## Circuit 1: Collections and invariants

- **Retrieval:** compare array, map, and set ownership/complexity tradeoffs.
- **Build:** group ordered tasks by owner without mutation.
- **Debug:** diagnose shared nested state between results.
- **Follow-up:** support streaming input too large for memory.

## Circuit 2: Async orchestration

- **Retrieval:** explain task versus microtask ordering and suspension.
- **Build:** implement a bounded concurrency mapper.
- **Debug:** find an unhandled rejection and leaked timer.
- **Follow-up:** add cancellation and collect-all error behavior.

## Circuit 3: Type-safe state

- **Retrieval:** contrast `unknown`, `any`, and a validated domain value.
- **Build:** model a request lifecycle as a discriminated union.
- **Debug:** remove an assertion hiding malformed JSON.
- **Follow-up:** evolve the union for older consumers.

## Circuit 4: React state ownership

- **Retrieval:** distinguish server, derived, URL, and ephemeral UI state.
- **Build:** design optimistic card rename with rollback.
- **Debug:** older response overwrites a newer edit.
- **Follow-up:** two tabs receive realtime changes while one has a draft.

## Circuit 5: Accessible interaction

- **Retrieval:** explain accessible name, role, focus, and status announcement.
- **Build:** create a keyboard alternative to drag-and-drop.
- **Debug:** focus disappears after list reorder.
- **Follow-up:** support reduced motion and touch without separate behavior rules.

## Circuit 6: HTTP contract

- **Retrieval:** classify safe and idempotent methods.
- **Build:** design a card-create endpoint including failures.
- **Debug:** response status and body disagree with OpenAPI.
- **Follow-up:** a mobile client remains on the old response shape for a month.

## Circuit 7: Retry-safe creation

- **Retrieval:** distinguish retry, deduplication, and idempotency.
- **Build:** define idempotency records and state transitions.
- **Debug:** database commits but response and completion record are lost.
- **Follow-up:** three application instances receive duplicates concurrently.

## Circuit 8: Pagination under change

- **Retrieval:** explain why a total order needs a tie-breaker.
- **Build:** write a descending composite cursor predicate.
- **Debug:** tied records duplicate between pages.
- **Follow-up:** cursor format and sort options evolve compatibly.

## Circuit 9: ASP.NET Core pipeline

- **Retrieval:** explain transient, scoped, singleton, and hosted lifetimes.
- **Build:** sketch endpoint-to-domain-to-data boundaries.
- **Debug:** scoped database context is captured by a singleton worker.
- **Follow-up:** propagate cancellation and trace context through background work.

## Circuit 10: Relational modeling

- **Retrieval:** map domain cardinality to keys and constraints.
- **Build:** model boards, memberships, columns, and ordered cards.
- **Debug:** concurrent moves create duplicate positions.
- **Follow-up:** add soft deletion and audit without leaking hidden records.

## Circuit 11: Query performance

- **Retrieval:** explain selectivity, composite index order, and write cost.
- **Build:** propose an index from one query and workload.
- **Debug:** plan ignores an apparently relevant index.
- **Follow-up:** one tenant becomes 1,000× hotter than the median.

## Circuit 12: Test strategy

- **Retrieval:** choose the cheapest faithful boundary for five risks.
- **Build:** define a testing pyramid for card movement.
- **Debug:** browser test fails only in parallel CI.
- **Follow-up:** halve suite duration while preserving confidence claims.

## Circuit 13: Evidence-driven debugging

- **Retrieval:** describe a hypothesis ledger and discriminating experiment.
- **Build:** create three ranked hypotheses from a latency symptom.
- **Debug:** new logging makes the symptom disappear.
- **Follow-up:** design lower-perturbation evidence and a regression check.

## Circuit 14: Authentication and authorization

- **Retrieval:** distinguish identity, role, membership, and resource policy.
- **Build:** define an actor/resource/action matrix.
- **Debug:** private title is loaded before forbidden response.
- **Follow-up:** membership is revoked during an open editing session.

## Circuit 15: Reliability and overload

- **Retrieval:** explain deadlines, backoff, jitter, and backpressure.
- **Build:** design a bounded worker queue.
- **Debug:** retries amplify a slow dependency outage.
- **Follow-up:** preserve the most valuable behavior while shedding load.

## Circuit 16: Events and outbox

- **Retrieval:** contrast database transaction and message delivery guarantees.
- **Build:** design write + outbox + publisher + consumer.
- **Debug:** duplicate and older events reach the consumer.
- **Follow-up:** evolve event schema while consumers deploy independently.

## Circuit 17: Observability

- **Retrieval:** compare logs, metrics, and traces.
- **Build:** instrument one critical journey and define an alert.
- **Debug:** request ID cannot cross an async boundary.
- **Follow-up:** reduce cost and cardinality without losing diagnosis.

## Circuit 18: Deployment and migration

- **Retrieval:** explain artifact identity and expand-and-contract.
- **Build:** plan a rolling field rename plus database migration.
- **Debug:** new release is healthy but incompatible with old workers.
- **Follow-up:** choose rollback or roll-forward during partial data migration.

## Circuit 19: System design

- **Retrieval:** explain how workload shape changes architecture.
- **Build:** design a collaborative board from requirements to operations.
- **Debug:** identify three vague or unsupported guarantees.
- **Follow-up:** redesign only the first bottleneck at 100× traffic.

## Circuit 20: Portfolio and behavioral evidence

- **Retrieval:** distinguish demonstrated, tested, measured, reviewed, and assumed.
- **Build:** present a five-minute case study and failure demo.
- **Debug:** audit two overstated résumé claims.
- **Follow-up:** tell a conflict/failure story emphasizing personal action and learning.

## Interviewer prompt deck

Use one unexpected prompt after the candidate’s initial answer:

1. What are you assuming?
2. What is the smallest counterexample?
3. How would you prove that claim?
4. What fails first at 10× scale?
5. What happens if the response is lost after commit?
6. What can an unauthorized user infer?
7. How do old and new versions coexist?
8. Which part would you remove first?
9. What would make you choose the rejected alternative?
10. How would an operator know this is failing?
11. How would a keyboard-only user complete it?
12. What did you personally implement or decide?

## Solo review protocol

After recording a circuit, wait at least one hour and mark:

- claims without evidence;
- answers that skipped clarification;
- jargon without mechanism;
- unhandled failure or concurrency paths;
- points where code was edited before a hypothesis;
- moments when a diagram or example would improve clarity;
- one answer to repeat after two days with a changed constraint.

| 6–10 | | | | |

# Thirty-Project SWE Ladder

These projects turn isolated skills into progressively broader evidence. Start
at the first level where you cannot meet the exit gate independently. Projects
may use RelayBoard’s domain or another domain, but keep the named engineering
constraint.

## Common project contract

Every project includes:

- a problem statement, user, success measure, and non-goal;
- acceptance criteria written before implementation;
- at least one automated behavior check;
- a deliberately exercised boundary or failure;
- a focused commit history;
- a short explanation of choice, alternative, and evidence;
- a delayed variation completed without copying the first version.

## Level 1: One-hour components

| # | Project | Hard constraint | Required evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Non-empty value factory | distinguish blank, missing, and invalid type | table tests and precise failures |
| 2 | Stable group-by utility | preserve order and input immutability | mutation and boundary checks |
| 3 | Retry classifier | only retry selected transient failures | fake-time sequence and stop evidence |
| 4 | Structured event builder | reserved fields and recursive redaction | parseable output and hostile inputs |
| 5 | Cursor codec | opaque versioned payload with validation | round trip, malformed, and old-version tests |
| 6 | Async concurrency limiter | bounded active work and ordered results | measured maximum concurrency |

Level 1 exit: implement any two in 45 minutes each, explain failures, and adapt
one to a changed input model the next day.

## Level 2: Half-day vertical behaviors

| # | Project | Hard constraint | Required evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 7 | Accessible validated form | keyboard, focus, field and summary errors | component test plus keyboard walkthrough |
| 8 | Paginated list endpoint | tied sort values and mutation between pages | real HTTP and data integration checks |
| 9 | Idempotent create handler | duplicate, mismatch, concurrent call, expiry | single-effect proof and state timeline |
| 10 | Versioned update | reject stale write without silent overwrite | two-client conflict demonstration |
| 11 | Health endpoint set | distinguish live, ready, degraded, starting | dependency failure matrix |
| 12 | Request correlation slice | propagate ID through HTTP, data, and event | trace reconstructed from logs only |

Level 2 exit: another developer can run the behavior from its contract and
diagnose the seeded failure without reading implementation first.

## Level 3: One- to three-day services

| # | Project | Hard constraint | Required evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 13 | Board query service | authorization, cursor pagination, query plan | non-disclosure test and plan comparison |
| 14 | Durable job worker | bounded queue, retry, cancellation, shutdown | load and interrupted-work report |
| 15 | Session lifecycle service | issuance, expiry, rotation, revocation | theft/revocation scenario matrix |
| 16 | Outbox publisher | atomic data+record, duplicate publication | crash-point simulation |
| 17 | Realtime reconnect service | checkpoint, missed events, stale versions | disconnect/reconnect trace |
| 18 | Schema evolution rehearsal | old/new apps coexist through migration | compatibility and rollback table |

Level 3 exit: reproduce one concurrency or partial-failure defect, implement a
durable mitigation, and explain the actual delivery or consistency guarantee.

## Level 4: One-week product slices

| # | Project | Hard constraint | Required evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 19 | Accessible task board | complete keyboard journey and async states | browser tests and manual audit |
| 20 | Collaborative card move | optimistic UI, conflict, realtime ordering | two-client recovery demo |
| 21 | Secure board sharing | invitation, membership, revocation, no leakage | adversarial authorization suite |
| 22 | Search and activity feed | query scale, cursor navigation, retention | plans, load profile, archive decision |
| 23 | Production delivery slice | build, deploy, health, telemetry, rollback | identified artifact and rehearsal |
| 24 | Incident-ready service | seeded latency, alert, diagnosis, runbook | timed incident and postmortem |

Level 4 exit: a reviewer can trace one user action across UI, API, database, and
telemetry; trigger a failure; and follow the documented recovery.

## Level 5: Multi-week portfolio systems

### 25. RelayBoard production capstone

Build the full capstone in [the main brief](../capstone/README.md). Hard
constraint: collaboration remains correct across retries, conflicts, reconnects,
authorization changes, and rolling delivery. Evidence: full case study, live or
recorded demo, tests, telemetry, ADRs, runbook, and review history.

### 26. Multi-tenant issue tracker

Organizations, projects, issues, comments, search, and audit history. Hard
constraint: tenant isolation at every query and cache boundary. Add export and
deletion workflows, role changes, rate limits, and an isolation threat model.

### 27. Notification delivery platform

Accept notification commands, schedule delivery, retry providers, record
outcomes, and expose user preferences. Hard constraint: duplicate commands and
provider uncertainty never create uncontrolled repeat effects. Measure queue
age, success, retry, and dead-letter behavior.

### 28. Reservation system

Search inventory, hold a slot, confirm payment-like intent, expire holds, and
cancel. Hard constraint: concurrent users cannot oversell capacity. Explain
transaction, lock/version, idempotency, timeout, and compensation choices.

### 29. Feature-flag service

Manage flags, environments, targeting rules, audit changes, and evaluate at
high read volume. Hard constraint: safe default and bounded staleness during
control-plane failure. Include rule validation, rollout, kill switch, caching,
and access controls.

### 30. Collaborative document outline

Edit and reorder outline nodes with multiple clients and offline periods. Hard
constraint: reconnect reconciles conflicts without silent data loss. Compare a
simple version-based approach with more advanced operation-merging only after
measuring actual requirements.

Level 5 exit: an unfamiliar reviewer can set up, operate, attack, observe,
recover, and question the system using its documented evidence.

## Apply multiple learning routes

For each project, complete at least four routes:

- map the system and failure paths;
- trace a concrete user example;
- state invariants and contracts;
- build a vertical slice test-first;
- explain and review the decision;
- diagnose an injected failure;
- transfer to a changed constraint.

Use the [ten-lens matrix](TEN-X-CHALLENGE-MATRIX.md) for advanced variations.

## Project review card

| Area | Question |
|---|---|
| Product | Which user outcome is demonstrably better? |
| Correctness | Which invariants survive boundary and concurrency cases? |
| Quality | Which risk is covered at which test boundary? |
| Security | What can an authenticated but unauthorized actor learn or change? |
| Reliability | What happens after partial success and lost acknowledgement? |
| Performance | Which measurement justifies the current design? |
| Operations | How is failure detected, diagnosed, and recovered? |
| Evolution | How do old and new versions coexist? |
| Communication | Which claims are tested, measured, reviewed, or assumed? |

# Tenfold SWE Training Expansion

This directory adds breadth and repetition without lowering the standard of the
main track. It is organized around ten engineering skill packs, 480 challenge
variants, progressively larger projects, interview circuits, and a 180-session
schedule.

Do not attempt everything in order. Use the
[starting diagnostic](../START-HERE-DIAGNOSTIC.md) and
[mastery rubric](../FEEDBACK-AND-MASTERY-RUBRIC.md) to select the weakest
high-value capability.

## Ten skill packs

1. [JavaScript runtime and asynchronous systems](tracks/01-javascript-runtime.md)
2. [TypeScript modeling and safe boundaries](tracks/02-typescript-modeling.md)
3. [React product engineering](tracks/03-react-product-engineering.md)
4. [HTTP, Node, and API engineering](tracks/04-api-engineering.md)
5. [C# and ASP.NET Core engineering](tracks/05-dotnet-engineering.md)
6. [SQL, data modeling, and persistence](tracks/06-data-engineering.md)
7. [Testing, debugging, and code review](tracks/07-quality-engineering.md)
8. [Distributed systems and architecture](tracks/08-distributed-systems.md)
9. [Security, delivery, and operations](tracks/09-production-engineering.md)
10. [System design, interviews, and career evidence](tracks/10-career-and-design.md)

Each pack includes:

- three explanations: analogy, system model, and invariant;
- visual or tabular representations with text equivalents;
- worked reasoning examples without a final project solution;
- guided, independent, debugging, and transfer challenges;
- teach-back and review prompts;
- a portfolio artifact and mastery gate.

## Large practice systems

- [Ten-lens challenge matrix](TEN-X-CHALLENGE-MATRIX.md): apply ten meaningful
  variations to each of the 48 micro-drills for 480 distinct exercises.
- [Project ladder](PROJECT-LADDER.md): move from one-hour utilities to
  production-shaped multi-week systems.
- [Interview circuits](INTERVIEW-CIRCUITS.md): repeatable coding, debugging,
  behavioral, API, database, frontend, operations, and system-design rounds.
- [180-session schedule](180-SESSION-PLAN.md): six phases with flexible
  15-, 30-, 60-, and 90-minute execution options.

## How to choose work

Use this decision rule:

| Evidence gap | Start with | Then transfer through |
|---|---|---|
| Cannot explain the core mechanism | a pack’s analogy and invariant | teach-back plus counterexample |
| Can explain but cannot implement | guided challenge | independent challenge without notes |
| Can implement only the happy path | debugging scenario | failure and concurrency lenses |
| Can solve familiar versions only | ten-lens matrix | a project with changed constraints |
| Can build but not demonstrate impact | portfolio artifact | interview circuit and claim audit |
| Broad weakness across several areas | 180-session plan | monthly diagnostic rerun |

## Common mastery contract

No activity is complete merely because code runs. Preserve:

1. a prediction made before execution;
2. a focused implementation or investigation;
3. automated or measured evidence;
4. one exercised failure, boundary, or adversarial case;
5. an explanation of the mechanism and tradeoff;
6. a delayed retry under a changed constraint;
7. a reviewable commit, diagram, decision, trace, or report.

## Suggested weekly mix

- one concept pass from a skill pack;
- two micro-drills, including one older topic;
- one base drill transformed by two challenge lenses;
- one capstone or project-ladder slice;
- one retrieval round;
- one review, teach-back, or interview simulation;
- one delayed reconstruction.

This mix deliberately crosses representations. It avoids turning a preferred
format into an excuse to avoid implementation, precise reading, speaking, or
collaboration.

## Tenfold reinforcement for every source

Use the [spaced-repetition trainer](../spaced-repetition/README.md) to generate
ten contextual cards for each file in both the core and expanded tracks. The
cards revisit a skill through reconstruction, implementation, diagnosis,
review, explanation, and transfer at widening intervals rather than treating a
completed pack as permanently learned.
